name: Hammer Curl
description: The hammer curl is performed with a neutral (hammer) grip throughout the full range of motion. This grip maximizes brachioradialis involvement and also provides strong brachialis stimulation. The neutral grip reduces wrist stress and builds forearm thickness alongside biceps development.

execution.starting_position: Stand or sit holding dumbbells at the sides with a neutral grip (thumbs pointing up). Elbows against the sides of the torso.
execution.setup_instructions: Keep the neutral grip throughout — do not rotate the wrist during the curl.
steps: Curl the dumbbell upward while maintaining the neutral grip.
Raise until the dumbbell is at shoulder height.
Lower under control back to the starting position.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale on the curl, inhale on the descent.
common_mistakes: Rotating the wrist to supinate — this turns it into a regular dumbbell curl
safety_considerations: The neutral grip is typically easier on the wrist than a supinated curl
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full extension at bottom, shoulder height at top.
coaching_cues: Keep thumbs pointing up throughout — think of hammering a nail
Squeeze the forearm and brachialis at the top
